why_it_matters: Board statement on pause; grandfathering of by-right/approved projects to be verified.

why_it_matters: GE Vernova 116 GW backlog, 2031 slots; Siemens Energy 3+ year lead times; relocation does not shorten power wait.

why_it_matters: Substation-class transformer lead times past 160 weeks; a switching-cost input.

headline: Data Centers on the Ballot tracker (daily review)
why_it_matters: Ballot measures and candidate pledges; cross-check with official election authorities before treating as binding.

headline: Hinojosa on CNN: "not that I hate data centers"; will seek laws and pause activity "until we have those protections"
why_it_matters: Tone softens to conditional/partnership framing; no change on the ladder (still a proposal, no EO until Jan 2027). Scope to permitted or under-construction projects remains unspecified; social-media claims that only new permits are covered are unverified.
affected: All Texas pipeline; ~25 GW reported under construction and 4.6 GW permitted per Modo Energy (industry estimate)

headline: Industry expects any Texas pause to run into mid-2027; Aurora, Modo Energy, GLJ estimates
why_it_matters: Houston Chronicle: Aurora Energy Research expects a pause to last to June/July 2027; GLJ Research estimates ~13 GW of Texas capacity exposed. Analyst estimates, not official.

headline: Democrats flip Georgia House (unofficial ~93 seats); GOP holds Senate 29-27
why_it_matters: Raises odds that cost-allocation or pause-supporting legislation clears the House in 2027; Senate stays a Republican check. Certification: counties Nov 9, state Nov 20.

headline: Kemp: no special session to curtail executive powers
why_it_matters: Removes near-term pre-emption risk to Governor-elect Bottoms' pledged executive pause; a budget-only session remains possible.

headline: Trenton Issue 17: effect on Prologis project under construction unclear; Amazon annexation could be refiled
why_it_matters: Grandfathering unresolved; mayor (resigning Jan 1) offers no policy direction. Results unofficial.
affected: Prologis Trenton (~250 MW reported); proposed AWS campus outside city limits

headline: Piqua: three commissioners recalled; city says effect of charter amendment on Meta project "unclear"
why_it_matters: Local permitting body reshaped; applicability to project underway undetermined.

headline: Lame-duck session Nov 10 - Dec 17; Sub. HB 646 recommitted to Senate Energy; advocates urge 12-month moratorium
why_it_matters: HB 646 (study commission, water reporting, large-load tariff, >250 MW generation requirement) could move in lame duck; moratorium ask is advocacy only, no sponsor.

headline: U.S. Senate agreed 62-21 to the motion to proceed to BAAJA (H.R. 2347 vehicle) on 10 Nov after 73-25 cloture on 9 Nov; final Senate passage expected week of 16 Nov; House concurrence still required
why_it_matters: Bill would require covered loads of 20 MW or more to pay full incremental grid costs and streamline NEPA/transmission permitting; weekend amendment narrows the behind-the-meter gas exemption to resources under 5 MW and adds a DOE technical-assistance program. Stage: motion to proceed agreed — not passed. Does not preempt state or local siting.
source_name: U.S. Senate roll call 258; Senate Daily Press; McGuireWoods; Center Square

headline: Bloomberg/Cleanview: ~40% of pending U.S. capacity sits in states whose governors-elect pledged pauses; BNEF counts 46 local measures
why_it_matters: Macro context only; statewide headlines are not applied to individual projects in the database.

headline: Data Centers on the Ballot tracker: 44 of 45 restriction counts complete; all 21 Ohio measures complete; no change in VA/OH/GA/TX since Nov 4
why_it_matters: Site displays a "simulated returns" preview banner; nothing certified. Cross-check with county boards before treating as binding.

headline: No confirmed material change; Loudoun formal pause resolution vote remains Nov 17; community marches in Hampton Roads and Roanoke
why_it_matters: Class D opposition without a specific instrument; Loudoun pause already in effect since Sept 15.

headline: ERCOT issuing second-round information requests to ~80% of 257 developers; probing whether projects were downsized below 75 MW to avoid grid review
why_it_matters: Audit report due Dec 10, PUCT Dec 17; downsizing findings could reclassify projects. Pause on new 75 MW+ energizations continues.

headline: Lubbock P&Z unanimously sends 12 data-center regulations to council; first moratorium hearing Nov 10, 2 p.m.
why_it_matters: Ladder moves to 4 (committee approved); 90-day pause needs 6 of 7 votes after Dec 10 second hearing.

headline: Riot 10-Q names Anthropic as tenant of 910 MW Corsicana powered-land lease (15 yr, ~$28bn); phases Sep 2027 / Jan 2028 / Jul 2028
why_it_matters: Largest single Texas AI lease; existing ~1 GW interconnection limits exposure to the ERCOT pause but phase deliveries still depend on ERCOT/PUCT treatment.

headline: Dade County commissioner proposes 90-day data-center moratorium after Master Works signals ~300 MW interest; December vote
why_it_matters: First Dade instrument; new project row PRJ-GE-0859 (0-300 MW, no capex). Public meeting Nov 23.

headline: OpenAI publishes Project Camellia Community Compact; says it will work to keep project on schedule ahead of Nov 17 vote
why_it_matters: Voluntary commitments (full energy-cost coverage, closed-loop cooling, annual audit) are counter-evidence to opposition but not binding until written into conditions.

headline: Ohio legislators signal compromise possible on data-center rules but no lame-duck commitment (Reineke, DeMora, John, Isaacsohn)
why_it_matters: HB 646 components (cost coverage, sales-tax change) could move by Dec 31; probability 25%. Rhetoric index updated.

headline: NextEra-Dominion accept 101 of 117 SCC merger conditions; evidentiary hearing Nov 17 (PUR-2026-00112)
why_it_matters: Shared-infrastructure item: conditions could shape capital plan and large-load posture for the 54.9 GW Dominion queue; not a restriction.

headline: Data Centers on the Ballot tracker: all 21 Ohio counts unchanged since Nov 3-4; nothing certified; no VA/GA/TX measures
why_it_matters: No change vs Nov 6 copy; Ohio county boards certify by Nov 24 (statutory window).

headline: Amazon paid $99.8M for 23 acres at 44146 Wade Drive (Loudoun) for a 100-ft data center; no special exception filed yet
why_it_matters: New land-controlled campus (PRJ-VI-0850). Any SE application would fall under the Loudoun pause if adopted Nov 17; staff already flagged height vs General Plan.

headline: Lordstown solicitor recommends extending the village data-center moratorium into 2027; mayor says ruling does not preclude a future data center
why_it_matters: Moratorium (EV-OH-0258) expires Dec 31; extension now recommended but not voted. Ladder unchanged at 5 (adopted).

headline: Conserve Ohio reports 150,000+ signatures toward a constitutional amendment banning data centers above 25 MW (400,000+ needed)
why_it_matters: Petition stage only (EV-OH-0266, ladder 1); earliest ballot Nov 2027. No legal effect today.

headline: Long County P&Z public hearing and vote on a proposed temporary data-center moratorium set for Nov 16
why_it_matters: Proposed (EV-GE-0168, ladder 2); no project in the county. Adds to coastal-Georgia pause cluster around Project Camellia.

headline: DeKalb County BOC Nov 10 agenda: review of health/environmental study required before the data-center moratorium can be lifted
why_it_matters: Catalyst for EV-GE-0077 (moratorium to 2027-03-30); lifting is conditional on the study review.

headline: Backfill: Morgan County 120-day data-center application moratorium (July 7; extension on Oct 20 agenda) and City of Madison pause to Nov 30
why_it_matters: Previously unlogged adopted instruments (EV-GE-0166/0167). Madison expiry Nov 30 is a live catalyst; Morgan extension unverified.

headline: CoreWeave letter to Gov.-elect Hinojosa seeks cooperation on data-center policy; Fort Worth confirms Nov 10 work session and first moratorium hearing

why_it_matters: No certified result yet; Ohio county certification due ~Nov 24.

headline: Effingham commissioners Burdette and Helmly put on record conditions for Project Camellia site plan (berm, wetlands, water, power); Helmly to bring moratorium discussion to Nov 17 meeting
why_it_matters: Local permitting authority for the OpenAI/Octans Effingham campus is now attaching explicit, quotable conditions; a county moratorium discussion on Nov 17 would be stage 2 (proposed) and would not by itself bind a project with an approved site plan.
affected: PRJ Effingham Project Camellia (OpenAI/Octans) - site plan vote Nov 17; EV-GE-0087 (possible county moratorium) unchanged at stage 2

headline: Oncor Q3 8-K: 795 large-load transmission requests incl. ~293 GW from data centers; ERCOT conditionally classified ~24 GW of Oncor load as base (10 GW already energized) and ~21 GW as studied, pending the December audit; 2027-31 capital plan heading ~20% higher
why_it_matters: Primary-source utility disclosure sizing the Oncor (DFW/West Texas) piece of the ERCOT queue; the 24 GW base + 21 GW studied classification is the realistic near-term envelope versus a 293 GW request figure that is not a forecast. Batch Zero projects are excluded from the base capital plan, so transmission for them is not yet funded or scheduled (final plan fall 2027). Class E infrastructure; no change to any single campus.
affected: Shared-infrastructure exposure for Oncor-territory campuses (Dallas-Fort Worth, Abilene/Stargate, Midland-Odessa, Lubbock); EV-TE-0308 Batch Zero note updated
source_name: Oncor 8-K Ex. 99.1 (SEC EDGAR); Dallas Express via Yahoo Finance

headline: Texas 2027 bill pre-filing opens: SB 293 (Huffman, Finance chair; majority of Senate as joint authors) would repeal data-center sales-tax exemptions, ending existing exemptions on effective date; HB 928 would require city/county votes for every data center; ~12 other data-center bills filed
why_it_matters: First concrete legislative instruments of the post-election Texas backlash; cost (not siting) exposure for all Texas campuses if SB 293 passes; ladder 3 (introduced), session opens 12 Jan 2027.
affected: All Texas campuses (cost); prospective siting for post-Sept-2027 applications (HB 928)
source_name: Texas Legislature Online; FOX 26; Dallas Morning News

headline: SpaceX proposes $24 bn gas-fired power plant and super-compute facility on 444 acres at Starbase (Cameron County); Chapter 312/380 incentives hearing 9 Dec, 7 p.m.
why_it_matters: New behind-the-meter hyperscale project sidesteps the ERCOT energization queue; tests whether the TCEQ permit pause and 2027 incentive repeal bills reach on-site-generation projects. Notice only; nothing approved.
source_name: City of Starbase notice; Reuters; Bloomberg

headline: Second Effingham lawsuit (State Court, filed ~6 Nov) alleges civil racketeering/conspiracy by county officials, IDA, OpenAI and Octans GA over Project Camellia land deal; seeks punitive damages
why_it_matters: Adds litigation pressure a week before the 17 Nov site-plan vote and moratorium discussion; damages suit does not itself seek to void approvals.

headline: Twin Township (Darke County) trustees adopt data-center definitions; 12-month moratorium vote set for 4 Dec (WHIO) / as early as 14 Dec (WDTN); no project proposed
why_it_matters: Continues the post-election wave of pre-emptive township moratoria; no capacity affected.

headline: Adams County BOE certified the Nov 3 results: Sprigg Twp zoning plan 332-301, Monroe Twp 149-102 (Official Canvass; certification form signed 11/09/2026)
why_it_matters: First county-certified results in the four-state coverage. Zoning adoption lets both AWS-evaluation townships regulate land use; it is not a ban until restrictive text is adopted. SoS statewide certification due by Dec 4.
affected: PRJ-OH-0371 AWS Adams County; PRJ-OH-0373; PRJ-OH-0374
source_name: Adams County Board of Elections (PDF viewed)

headline: Butler County Planning Commission unanimously recommended St. Clair Township zoning amendment prohibiting data centers as a principal use in all districts
why_it_matters: Second advisory approval for a permanent prohibition on the St. Clair portion of the AWS ~600-acre Madison/St. Clair site; trustees say they will adopt (date TBD). County six-month moratorium on Madison Twp expires ~Dec 16.

headline: Fort Worth held first statutory hearing on 90-day data-center moratorium; DCIC delivered 19 recommendations; no vote (second hearing Jan 12, adoption vote Feb 16, 2027)
why_it_matters: Moratorium remains proposed (ladder 2). NBC DFW headline saying the city "approves" the moratorium is contradicted by the City page, WFAA, Fox 4, CBS and the Star-Telegram.
affected: Fort Worth pipeline incl. PRJ-TE-0565 Colovore Alliance ($430 mn permit filed)
source_name: Fort Worth Report; City of Fort Worth; WFAA

headline: Lubbock held first public hearing on a 90-day data-center moratorium; second hearing and first vote Dec 10
why_it_matters: Procedural step only; adoption needs 6 of 7 council votes. Council consideration of the 12 P&Z development standards reported for Dec 1 or Dec 8 (conflict).

headline: Botetourt judge overruled demurrers in FOIA suit against the Google (Helio Capital) performance agreement; hearing resumes Nov 16 with injunction request pending
why_it_matters: Suit seeking to void the June 2025 agreement and halt grading at Greenfield advances past the first dismissal attempt; pleas in bar under advisement. Resumption date reported as Nov 16 (WDBJ7, Virginia Business) or Nov 19 (WSET).
affected: PRJ-VI-0090 Google Botetourt (300 MW, under construction)

headline: Spanberger and General Assembly Democratic leaders unveiled a 2027 agenda to end by-right approval for data centers over 25 MW (local approval required regardless of prior approvals), ban NDAs, limit evaporative cooling in water-scarce areas and shift transmission costs
why_it_matters: Proposal by the governor and both chamber leaders in a Democratic trifecta (ladder 2; no bills filed; drafts due Dec 31; session Jan 13). Retroactivity language is the key unknown for by-right pipelines in Loudoun and Prince William. Not applied to individual project scores.

headline: JLARC: data-center sales-tax exemption was 60% of Virginia incentive spending over a decade ($4.5 bn FY2021-25) and returned 22 cents per dollar
why_it_matters: Strengthens the case for revisiting the exemption in 2027 (joint subcommittee Dec 15; session Jan 13). Study only; no change to the exemption, which runs under HB 30 with the 1.1 c/kWh consumption tax.
affected: All Virginia campuses using the exemption

headline: DeKalb County deferred data-center definitions resolution to Dec 15 and withdrew (5-2) a proposed independent health/environmental study; moratorium stays through Mar 30, 2027
why_it_matters: No change to the moratorium; the definitions vote on Dec 15 will shape what the post-moratorium rules cover.

headline: Second-day bill detail: SB 36 (Zaffirini) would bar new Ch. 380/381 agreements and Ch. 312 abatements for data centers from Sept 1, 2027; 23 of 31 senators reported backing SB 293 repeal
why_it_matters: Incentive-stripping bills now span sales-tax (SB 293/HB 167) and local abatements (SB 36). None restricts siting; effect is on project economics, not permits.
affected: Texas projects relying on Ch. 312/380/381 incentives

headline: Ohio lame duck: Senate President-presumptive Reineke would not commit to passing data-center rules this year; Conserve Ohio presses for a 12-month statutory moratorium; Sub. HB 646 still in Senate Energy
why_it_matters: No movement on HB 646 as of Nov 10; voting sessions run weekly through Dec 17. Statewide moratorium remains a demand, not a bill with momentum.

headline: Washington County, Va. supervisors unanimously adopted an ordinance requiring a special exception permit and two public hearings for any data center; in effect
why_it_matters: First data-center zoning language in the county; a review process, not a ban. No tracked projects; chair says none are seeking to locate there.

headline: Lee County extended its data-center moratorium (unincorporated areas) from Dec 31, 2026 to June 30, 2027; effective on adoption
why_it_matters: Second extension of a December 2025 moratorium while staff draft an ordinance; full resolution text published. No tracked projects.

headline: McIntosh County commissioners approved a zoning change requiring special use permits for data centers, described as a stopgap pending a policy white paper
why_it_matters: Adds mandatory public hearings and commission oversight on the Georgia coast; not a ban. No tracked projects.

headline: Brownsville Ordinance 2026-1826: 90-day data-center moratorium adopted 6-0 on second reading; in effect Nov 5 through Feb 3, 2027 (extension to ~May 18 expected; permanent ban discussed)
why_it_matters: Status correction: our log had carried Brownsville at the drafting stage. Covers city and ETJ; SpaceX Starbase land (de-annexed) is outside it.
affected: PRJ-TE-0671 Brownsville proposals; PRJ-TE-0860 Starbase (not covered)
source_name: City of Brownsville; OpenTexas meeting record; ValleyCentral

headline: ERCOT CEO Pablo Vegas said he will ask the Legislature for authority to require data-center curtailment at EEA level 1 (reserves <2,500 MW) or earlier, instead of level 2
why_it_matters: Request to lawmakers, not a rule or bill. Would raise the interruptibility data centers must plan for and the value of on-site backup; does not affect siting. Statewide; no project re-scored.

headline: Fort Worth City page: moratorium adoption vote is Feb 23, 2027 (second reading), not Feb 16; 90-day pause starts on adoption, ends May 24 (Aug 22 if extended)
why_it_matters: Schedule correction from the primary source; ladder unchanged (proposed). Second hearing and first reading remain Jan 12.

headline: More than a dozen environmental groups launched a "Pause to Protect" platform in Hanover calling for a statewide pause on data-center permits and grid connections; Chesapeake Bay Foundation now backs a moratorium
why_it_matters: Advocacy demand, not a government proposal; splits from the governor's agenda, which has no moratorium. Data Center Coalition opposed. DEQ water-scarcity-area report due this month.

headline: Fluidstack (formerly Solis Arx) Progress Park campus in Wythe County reported under construction; majority complete by end-2027; >$1 bn
why_it_matters: Stage change in the master: county described the project as under construction on Oct 27 and grading was observed; Preserve Wythe opposition noted. MW undisclosed.

headline: Goochland draft TOD amendments: prohibit data centers outside the overlay, keep by-right status in TOD North and Central, CUP in TOD West; Planning Commission Dec 16, Board possibly February
why_it_matters: Tightening at the margins; the by-right path for the Google West Creek site would remain under the draft. Residents demanded hearings for every project.
affected: PRJ-VI-0066 Google Goochland; PRJ-VI-0067 Tract; Tuckahoe Tech Park

headline: Rossford Planning Commission approved a special use permit and preliminary site plan for a 16 MW, $150 mn QLEVR LLC data center in Harmon Industrial Park; final site plan pending
why_it_matters: Small non-hyperscale approval in the Toledo area (new PRJ-OH-0861); shows permitting continuing for sub-25 MW projects after the Nov 3 votes.

headline: Senate: Thune filed cloture on the Capito substitute and on H.R. 2347 (permitting bill) on Nov 11; no final vote yet
why_it_matters: Cloture votes expected late this week or next; House concurrence still required. Nothing enacted.
